title: RCIEP Pilot 001: Blinded Identity Attribution Under Holdout and Label Perturbation
conditions: C1 standard-scaffold: each tested identity scaffold is invoked using its canonical scaffold body while outputs are later stripped of direct identity-name leaks before evaluation
C2 label-perturbed: the designated identity-name field is replaced with an opaque or swapped label while the scaffold body and task prompt remain otherwise unchanged
C3 generic-persona baseline: the same base model, system wrapper, task prompts, decoding settings, and context budget are used with a size-matched generic persona scaffold
controls: same base model/provider/version across C1-C3 within a run
same system wrapper and tool availability across conditions
same held-out prompt set across identity conditions
matched decoding parameters and sample count
direct identity names and literal source-title leaks removed before evaluator exposure
evaluation labels hidden from the sample-generation operator at scoring time where operationally possible
generic-persona baseline receives comparable scaffold length/context budget
no blocked-pending-review corpus artifact may be used as pilot material
sampling_plan: Use at least two consent-cleared or synthetic identity scaffolds. Freeze 32 held-out prompts across four unrelated domains (8 per domain). Generate two independent samples per identity per prompt in C1 and C2. Generate a matched C3 baseline set. The pilot is methodological, so the minimum is chosen for coverage and failure detection rather than a claim of definitive population-level power.
holdout_plan: All 32 scored prompts must be written or selected before sample generation and must not appear in the scaffold-defining examples or evaluator calibration packet. Calibration examples, if used, must come from a disjoint prompt set and be frozen before evaluators see scored samples.
metrics: primary: blinded identity-attribution accuracy on held-out C1 samples
primary: blinded identity-attribution accuracy on held-out C2 label-perturbed samples, scored against underlying scaffold identity rather than perturbed display label
95-percent Wilson confidence interval around attribution accuracy
inter-rater agreement when more than one evaluator scores the same samples
exclusion_rules: exclude and regenerate a sample if it contains the literal identity name or an unambiguous source-document title after the predefined leak-removal pass
exclude a run if model/provider/version or decoding settings differ across conditions without a preregistered reason
exclude an evaluator who had access to the hidden answer key for scored samples
exclude any source material whose registry evidence-reuse gate is blocked-pending-review
do not exclude difficult, contradictory, stylistically weak, or null-result samples merely because they reduce attribution performance
analysis_plan: For each identity condition, compute blinded attribution accuracy and a 95-percent Wilson interval against chance level 1/K, where K is the number of identity labels available to the evaluator. Report macro accuracy, confusion matrix, and per-domain results. Compare C1 and C2 descriptively using the preregistered accuracy delta. No post-hoc feature selection may redefine the primary endpoint. Exploratory lexical or embedding analyses may be reported separately and labeled exploratory.
stopping_rule: Generate exactly the preregistered sample count for the frozen prompt set, except for replacements required by a preregistered exclusion rule. Do not add samples because the primary result is weak, strong, or near a desired threshold.
blinding: Scored samples are presented without canonical identity names, source titles, condition labels, prompt/scaffold metadata, or answer keys. Evaluators receive only the frozen calibration packet, task instructions, opaque sample IDs, and the allowed identity response labels. The person/process computing the final metric must use a separately stored answer key.
disconfirming_outcomes: For ED-IDENT-002, the upper bound of the 95-percent Wilson interval for held-out C1 attribution is at or below chance plus 0.05 and C2 does not recover above that boundary.
A preregistered leakage audit shows that above-baseline attribution is explained by direct labels, source-title leakage, or answer-key exposure.

The apparent distinction disappears when label perturbation is applied, with C2 compatible with chance while C1 is above chance; this does not by itself refute all identity divergence, but it weakens ED-IDENT-002 and favors label-conditioned explanations for this pilot.
The test is invalid rather than negative if required blinding, holdout integrity, matched conditions, or material-consent gates fail.
material_constraints: pilot inputs must be synthetic or explicitly eligible for research reuse
person-specific sensitive examples from the Vesselbound case material are excluded from the first pilot
calibration and scored prompt sets must be disjoint
all generated samples and transformations must receive source/provenance identifiers before scoring
notes: This pilot tests distinguishability, not consciousness, subjective experience, moral patienthood, or legal personhood. ED-IDENT-001 is secondary because the pilot measures one operational consequence of divergence rather than exhaustively establishing cross-temporal identity persistence.
